text:
neil: @here security advisory: we detected multiple changed SSH host keys for the production bastion in the last 24h from our monitoring (fingerprint drift + unexpected restarts). No evidence of data exfil, but we need immediate verification and a controlled rotation. :lock:

neil: TL;DR - action items for infra owners (tara/devops): verify integrity, rotate host keys, publish new known_hosts, rotate deploy keys that touch bastion, and schedule a 30m maintenance window.

sec-alerts-bot: Alert 2026-04-18T03:12Z - Bastion hostkey mismatch (sha256:QwEr...): 3 changes in 24h across 2 AZs. Triggers: host-key-checker, instance-restart-watch.

tara: Thanks. I'll start with an integrity check on the instances and compare AMIs. Anyone running manual SSH sessions to bastion right now, please disconnect and avoid rekeying until we complete checks.

devops: If we need emergency rollback, can we redeploy the previous autoscaling group with the known-good AMI?

neil: Yes. Recovery plan: 1) isolate bastion in NACL (restrict ingress to eng IP ranges), 2) spin up a new bastion from known-good AMI (tag: ami-prod-bastion-20260401), 3) rotate host keys via our key-rotator job, 4) update SSM parameter with new known_hosts and notify teams.

mike: What about CI/deploy runners that have direct keys stored in secrets manager and SSH to the bastion to tunnel?

tara: Good call. Owners of any automation that uses deploy keys must rotate those keys and update secrets manager. We'll invalidate old deploy keys in 24h unless you file an exception with a mitigation plan.

neil: Required actions and deadlines:
- 2026-04-18 12:00 UTC: Infra/owners verify instance AMI checksums and confirm no unexpected AMI swaps. Reply in-thread with findings.
- 2026-04-19 00:00 UTC: Rotate bastion host keys and publish new known_hosts to SSM path /prod/bastion/known_hosts.
- 2026-04-19 06:00 UTC: Rotate any deploy keys that SSH to bastion; update Secrets Manager references.
- 2026-04-25: Remove any temporary exceptions; finalize postmortem.

neil: Quick commands we've used:
```bash
# check host key fingerprint via ssh-keyscan
ssh-keyscan -t rsa bastion.prod.redwood.internal | ssh-keygen -lf -

# list instances launched from unexpected AMIs
aws ec2 describe-instances --filters "Name=tag:role,Values=bastion" --query 'Reservations[].Instances[].[InstanceId,ImageId,State.Name,LaunchTime]' --output table

# lookup recent restarts in CloudWatch
aws logs filter-log-events --log-group-name /aws/ec2/instance-systems --filter-pattern "Restarted instance" --start-time $(date -d '1 day ago' +%s)000
```

devops: I'll prepare a new AMI bake and stand up a parallel bastion in the staging AZ to test key rotation. Will post AMI id here when ready.

ops-bot: Maintenance window suggestion: 2026-04-19T02:00Z-02:30Z (low traffic). Please acknowledge if this conflicts with scheduled deploys.

mike: We have a planned deploy 2026-04-19T02:05Z for payments team. I'll ask them to reschedule to avoid overlap.

tara: If you maintain any automation that uses port-forwarding through bastion (SSH socks), please update docs and client known_hosts after rotation. We'll provide a signed fingerprint file in SSM so clients can verify.

neil: For audit/forensics: collect /var/log/auth.log and journalctl for the last 48h and upload to the secure bucket s3://redwood-sec-audit/bastion-2141004321/. Use the upload helper: `tools/upload-audit --path /var/log/auth.log --dest bastion-2141004321`

devops: AMI bake complete: ami-0b7c9d5f (bastion-20260418). Spinning up test instance in us-west-2b now.

tara: Confirmed: two instances had a host key change around 03:10Z and both were in the same ASG but different AZs. No unknown AMI found; kernels match expected build. Suspected cause: automated image import pipeline triggered by a tag update. We're throttling that pipeline and will require manual approval going forward.

neil: Good work. Next steps: rotate keys during maintenance window, publish signed fingerprints, rotate deploy keys, and follow-up with a short postmortem by 2026-04-25. If you need help with key-rotator, ping me or devops.

ops-bot: Scheduled maintenance created: 2026-04-19T02:00Z-02:30Z. Notifying #eng and affected service owners.

mike: Acknowledged. I'll coordinate with payments to shift their deploy.

neil: Thanks all — if you see any anomalous access after rotation, escalate to pager and tag sec-oncall. We'll keep this thread updated.
